issue: gʷṓs te toy-kʷe 'you and your cattle': -kʷe lands on the possessive clitic toy while gʷṓs stands before te, so the second conjunct (gʷṓs toy) is split around the first; read te gʷṓs-kʷe toy.
nébʰōs as nom./acc. pl. of the neuter s-stem nébʰos: handbook plural is *nébʰesh₂ (Gk νέφεα); -ōs is only the disputed collective. pnéwmn̥ 'breath' is a Greek-only derivative.
Pre-laryngeal scholarly title: owis eḱwōs kʷe with no laryngeals or accents and kʷe written as a separate word; in corpus notation h₂ówis h₁éḱwōs-kʷe.
wóǵʰōs (nom./voc. pl.) after ní for 'sat down on the wagon': needs loc. sg. wóǵʰey (or acc. wóǵʰom). Also h₁íd (neut.) in 'and it led her away' does not match masc. wóǵʰos if the wagon is meant.
méǵh₂s h₁ésmi: masc. predicate adjective for the Sun, which is neuter sóh₂wl̥ and is otherwise referred to with neuter h₁íd; expect méǵh₂. Also nébʰōs (see the s-stem plural note).

gʷéwi (loc. sg. of gʷṓws) in 'Drive the cattle to it!': needs acc. pl. gʷṓs. Minor: séh₁mn̥ dʰoHnéh₂m-kʷe is 'seed and grain', not the English apposition; h₁léwdʰis sg. with h₂wéyst and then 3pl gʷh₂ént.
déh₃noybʰos (dat./abl. pl.) as the object of dédh₃n̥ti 'give her a gift': needs acc. déh₃nom.

Pre-laryngeal scholarly line (tod ḱeḱluwōs owis aǵrom ebʰuget): no laryngeals, a-vowel in aǵrom, augmented ebʰuget, no accents. In corpus notation tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis h₂éǵrom bʰugét or similar. The sense is right.

h₂élēth₁es is SBJV.2DU, but the English is 'If I do not nourish it': needs 1sg h₂éloh₂/h₂élōh₂. Also mē in a conditional protasis (expect ne), and dédh₃te 2pl addressed to two gods where 2du dédh₃th₁es exists.
Two present stems of 'lie' in one sentence: légʰyonti (yé-present) next to légʰete (thematic, used for the future 'you will lie').
gʷṓs moy moy h₂ew wédʰe: two adjacent moy enclitics (gen. 'my' + dat. 'to me'). Grammatical but awkward; a stressed dat. méǵʰye for 'to me' would be clearer.
Pre-laryngeal scholarly title owis eḱwōskʷe: no laryngeals or accents; in corpus notation h₂ówis h₁éḱwōs-kʷe.
deywóh₁ (nom. du./ins. sg.) as the subject of 3sg h₁ért 'a god came': needs nom. sg. deywós. Also 'Since then' in the last English sentence has no PIE counterpart.
